tapeLine: Latest sourced close is Thursday 15 October, after a hot September PPI: Dow +1.08% to 52,177.69, S&P 500 +0.3% to 7,744.81 (one outlet gives 7,744.06), Nasdaq +0.1% to 26,713.03, per Investing.com and Seeking Alpha. No Friday futures were found.
matters:
Thursday's September PPI rose 1.3% on the month, the largest monthly rise in about four and a half years, against forecasts of roughly 0.3-0.6% that varied by outlet; core PPI rose 0.7% on the month, per Seeking Alpha (15 Oct). Retail sales were due the same morning; no result was found.

Stocks recovered from early losses as Treasury yields fell: Fed rate-hike expectations rose after the data, then the rise was erased as bonds rallied, per Investing.com (15 Oct). Eight of 11 S&P sectors rose, led by healthcare; energy lagged. The Nasdaq 100 had been more than 5% below its record at the lows, per the same report.

Invalidation: whether the S&P 500 reclaims Friday 9 October's 7,811.54 record close, and whether yields keep falling after a PPI print this far above forecast.
alsoOnTape: Oil, gold and Treasury yield levels were not found with a dated source and are not carried.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Thursday 15 October: Dow +1.08% to 52,177.69, S&P 500 +0.3% to 7,744.81, Nasdaq +0.1% to 26,713.03, per Investing.com. Friday futures not found.
macro: Data — September PPI (15 Oct): +1.3% m/m vs ~0.3-0.6% forecast depending on outlet; core +0.7% m/m, per Seeking Alpha. September retail sales and jobless claims results were not found. CPI on Wednesday was +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y, per CNBC (14 Oct).
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: Indexes rebounded Thursday despite a much hotter PPI, as yields fell; the S&P 500 remains about 0.9% below its 7,811.54 record close.
regime.sizing: The 27-28 October FOMC is the next scheduled evidence; no Friday data release was confirmed.

secondOrder: Two energy-led inflation prints in two days produced opposite equity reactions: Wednesday's CPI sold off, Thursday's larger PPI surprise was bought once bonds rallied. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior read that PPI and retail sales were the next evidence on energy-led price pressure: PPI confirmed it (+1.3% m/m), but the implied pressure on equities did not follow, with all three indexes closing higher, per Investing.com.
The prior invalidation level held: the S&P 500 did not recover 7,811.54; it closed Thursday at 7,744.81, per Investing.com.
The prior note that rate-hike bets were reviving was borne out only briefly: they rose after PPI and were erased the same session as bonds rallied, per Investing.com.
Whether yields rose into CPI cannot be graded: no sourced yield levels were found.
The 27-28 October FOMC has not occurred.
